newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end down in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end down in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in slow trading on Friday with major institutions staying on the sidelines after prices trended downward over the last few trading days, traders said.
The most actively traded January 1998 contract fell nine yuan to 3,311 yuan ($399) per tonne. It opened at an intraday high of 3,330 yuan and hit a low of 3,310 yuan.
July lost 30 yuan to 3,230, September fell eight to 3,290, November 24 to 3,296 and March 1998 64 to 3,211.
Combined volume fell to 10,500 tonnes from 17,800.
Traders said a downtrend that started on Tuesday sidelined major institutions on Friday, and the shrinking volume indicated most investors were waiting for prices to fall further.
"The key September contract is likely to find support at the 3,260-yuan level in the short term and investors are expected to build positions around that level," one analyst said.
